significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that a weak or absent verb-to-complement "factivity gate" causes the specific failure to distinguish "X knows that P" from "X believes that P," and that strengthening this pathway repairs factivity judgments; this is a form-(ii) causal claim rather than a law relating independently measurable quantities. It would establish both a phenomenon—the missing "induced shift" in complement-truth encoding—and a mechanism involving information routed from the factive verb, materially constraining explanations of this one semantic failure but not predicting other belief or knowledge behaviors; resources such as FactBank and MegaVeridicality show that verb-conditioned factuality is a structured phenomenon, but do not make this proposed mechanism a broader law. A negative result showing a robust factive shift would rule out the absent-gate explanation, although failure to localize one would not distinguish a diffuse mechanism from no mechanism, especially because "weak/absent" is somewhat underspecified. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on internal belief states would not retain this score; the factivity-specific causal account earns the topic-median score, but its single-behavior gate-plus-repair form does not justify moving above that baseline.

reach.justification: The named handles are the measurable "induced shift in the internal truth encoding," attention heads carrying the factive signal, and a "factivity steering vector" or amplified pathway that could be used to alter judgments. The diagnostic is mainly post hoc, while the steering intervention can act before a model produces a factivity judgment, but the claim does not establish that gate strength forecasts failures in advance across unrelated cases. After recalibration on another model, the conclusion supplies a procedure for finding a new pathway rather than a transferable quantitative relation predicting what that model will contain; its asserted scope is LLMs across sizes and base versus instruction-tuned checkpoints, with uptake primarily among interpretability and semantic-evaluation researchers rather than general deployment practitioners. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score—the specific diagnostic and intervention add reusable value beyond merely studying LLM beliefs—but they remain close to the topic's default probe-plus-steering deliverable.
